name: Smile (1985)
description: PSA's scheme of the 1980s, worn by its jets until the 1988 merger into USAir: white over a bare metal belly, with three bands of light orange, orange and red under a white pinstripe, the windows in the top one. The bands wrap the whole nose below the black anti-glare panel, the nose cap is black, and a black smile curls up each side of the chin from the nose gear to the top of the red band. Behind the smile the belly is bare metal. On the white fin the same three bands sweep up from the root behind the leading edge and run aft under the tailplane. 'PSA' in white wide capitals outlined and shadowed in black, ahead of the wing above the windows and low on the fin.

logos.description: The smile: one black stroke about 15-20 cm wide, the corner of a grin seen from the side. It starts at the top of the red band about 3.1 m back from the nose, runs nearly straight down, then curves forward to end under the chin at the nose gear about 2 m back. Seen from ahead the two sides make a U under the nose. The red band's lower edge and the white pinstripe follow its aft side down, so the paint is ahead of it and the bare metal belly behind.

titles.style: PSA's wordmark: wide, squarish capitals leaning slightly forward, white with a black outline and a heavy black shadow dropped down and back, so from a distance it reads as black.
PSA's wordmark: wide, squarish capitals leaning slightly forward, white with a black outline and a heavy black shadow dropped down and back, so from a distance it reads as black.

notes: Measured 2026-11-24 for Skyarium's ghost flights, on the MD-82 (shapes/MD82.json), which also stands in for PSA's DC-9-30s (the same nose and paint). PSA's code PSA is now PSA Airlines', so it's keyed PS1949 (founded 1949). No side-on photo was found: N944PS (sourceRefs 0) is seen from a terminal at an angle, so it was fitted twice with tools/photo_trace.py (the cabin by its first and last windows, the tail by the tail cone, fin tip and aft door), heights read against the cabin windows. The bands' edges are constant heights on the aircraft (light orange 0.60 m to 0.04 m above the cabin's centerline, orange to -0.27 m, red to -0.50 m, the white pinstripe to -0.65 m), level and straight from the tail to just behind the flight deck, as the photos show them, including past the wing root. They're converted to the MD-82's outline and thinned to the fewest points that draw within 3 mm of that line. So their y rises where the outline's belly takes in the wing-body fairing (x 0.51-0.66) and the tail cone. That's the frame's bulge, not the paint's. Round the nose the edges are smooth curves (Catmull-Rom through a few points, sampled every 5 cm). The red band's lower edge and the pinstripe follow the smile's aft side at a fixed offset. On the fin each band edge is a straight run up from the swoosh's point at the root, a quadratic arc and a level run aft, fitted to the traced edges within about 0.02 of the fin. The nose (the bands' curve down round it, the anti-glare panel, the smile's place) is by eye from N924PS and N952PS against the door and flight deck windows, good to about 0.3 m. Heights good to about 0.05 of the side, positions along the body to about 0.3 m. Uncertain: when the scheme began (it's on the MD-80s from delivery in 1980-81, so `from` is left out); on N952PS (1987, right side) the windows sit just above the light orange and the lower nose under the pinstripe looks bare, where the 1981-85 photos show the windows in the band and the chin painted ahead of the smile (drawn as those); N944PS's nose cap is orange, the others' black (drawn black). The stabilizer's color is a guess (white). PSA's BAe 146s (1984-88) are drawn on shapes/B462.json (types.B462: the bands under the windows, see its note).

B462.note: On the BAe 146 the bands run under the windows, not through them: the windows are in the white, and the light orange, orange and red bands (0.27, 0.26 and 0.25 m deep) and the white pinstripe (0.11 m) run level from the tail cone, where the belly's rise cuts them off, to the black nose cap, the top edge meeting the nose's outline about 0.9 m back. There's no black anti-glare panel. Ahead of the smile the red runs down to the chin; behind it the pinstripe follows the smile's aft side down and the belly is bare metal. On the fin the three bands sweep up from a point near the root behind a bare metal leading edge, the top edge almost parallel to the leading edge and the bottom one diagonal, and run level aft under the top fairing (fin height shares 0.36 to 0.70). The nacelles are polished metal (pylons white). Titles: 'PSA' above the windows aft of the forward door (5.4-7.9 m back) and low on the fin. Measured on N356PS (1986, right side, side-on, the only side-on photo found), checked on N351PS, N366PS (1987, right side), N348PS (1987, left side) and N350PS (1986, right side). Edges are fitted: level runs converted to the B462 outline and thinned to the fewest points that draw within 3 mm; the smile's aft side from the mark itself; on the fin each edge a straight run, a quadratic arc and a level run. Heights good to about 0.05 m along the cabin; the nose, the smile's place and the fin's swoosh to about 0.2 m. The shape itself is low confidence (an enthusiast's schematic).
